name: Cotton thread making at Neolithic Mehrgarh
summary: Mineralised cotton threads survive in a copper bead from a Neolithic burial at Mehrgarh, Balochistan.
description: Researchers identified mineralised threads inside a copper bead from grave MR.84.03.158 as cotton using reflected-light and scanning electron microscopy. Copper corrosion preserved the threads. Their structure identifies the genus Gossypium; the cotton species, whether it was domesticated and the spinning implement remain unknown.

impact.note: Scored on the general view, not on the cited page: cotton cloth from South Asia came to clothe the subcontinent and was traded and copied across Asia, Africa and Europe (depth 2), and calico printing and mechanised spinning grew from the effort to match it (generativity 2); reach is held at 2, not the lead's 3, because cotton was taken up separately in the Americas and Africa and the lower score is taken when torn.

date.label: c. 5250–4650 cal BCE (Mehrgarh Period I context)
date.basis: Moulherat et al. placed grave MR.84.03.158 in Period I and used the then-current first-half sixth-millennium BCE estimate. Mutin et al. dated the Period I sequence to about 5250–4650 cal BCE from human teeth in the cemetery.

events.statement: Researchers identified cotton threads preserved within a copper bead from aceramic Neolithic grave MR.84.03.158 at Mehrgarh.

evidence.locator: pp. 1393–1396, Introduction and Description of the Beads, Figs. 2, 4, 7–9; pp. 1398–1400
evidence.supports: Identifies bead MR.84.03.158.01b and grave MR.84.03.158, assigns the burial to the aceramic Neolithic Period I and reports Gossypium threads.

evidence.locator: pp. 3–4, Fig. 2 and Discussion: The dating and duration of Mehrgarh Period I
evidence.supports: The newer cemetery model estimates about 5250–4650 cal BCE for Period I on the basis of enamel measurements on other archaeological material from the cemetery.

events.caveats: The range dates the Period I context. The bead and thread have no reported direct date, and grave 158 has not been securely matched to a dated tooth. No woven cloth survives in the bead.

earliest_record.rationale: The bead is the dated contextual witness to cotton thread at Mehrgarh. The displayed range reflects the Period I chronology.

unresolved.note: Match grave MR.84.03.158 to the cemetery stratigraphic levels or an independently dated sample to narrow the artefact context within Period I.
The cotton species, wild or domesticated status, spinning tools and geographic source of the thread remain unestablished.
The Shahi Tump string, Mohenjo-daro cloth and Tel Tsaf and Dhuweila fibre finds are distinct witnesses. A Mehrgarh connection needs evidence of material provenance or a shared technical sequence.

research.note: The original 2002 paper supplies the grave, bead and fibre identification. The 2025 enamel study revises the contextual phase chronology. The copper bead was made from rolled sheet; the later Mehrgarh lost-wax amulet is a different product and method.
